hypothesis.title: Carrier Choice Changes Phrase Agency
hypothesis.question: When notes, tempo, and harmony are held constant, do changes in the carrier layer alter perceived agency, tension, and direction?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If a fixed call-and-response phrase is presented through different carrier layers, then listeners will report different perceived agency and tension because carrier structures define adjacency, timing, transmission, and perceptual support before the foreground message is interpreted.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: The Tonnetz source shows that harmonic objects gain motion from an underlying adjacency graph, so the carrier space changes what counts as a small or meaningful move [S1]. David Mayer's call-and-response practice treats silence, contrast, and timbral layering as structural supports for dialogue, implying that the gap and layer carrying a phrase can change its expressive identity [S2]. LoRa chirp spread spectrum demonstrates that audio communication depends on the modulation carrier and bandwidth/energy budget, while UAF's 600 ms chunks show that audio pipelines impose temporal carrier units that can introduce latency or information loss [S3][S5]. The infrasound source adds a threshold case where acoustic energy may shape experience without being heard as ordinary pitch [S4]. The HHL music-generation proposal further suggests that musical distributions can depend on coherent consumption before measurement, making collapse or block boundaries part of the compositional carrier [S6].

recipe.title: Same Message, Four Carriers
recipe.bodyMd: Create a two-bar call-and-response phrase and keep its MIDI notes, tempo, velocities, and base harmony unchanged across all renders. Version A uses a graph carrier: voice the answer by nearest harmonic adjacency inspired by Tonnetz traversal [S1]. Version B uses a silence carrier: render three response gaps of 0 ms, 300 ms, and 600 ms, treating silence as the medium that carries dialogue [S2][S5]. Version C uses a chirp carrier: route the answer through a rising bandpass or pitch-swept layer, borrowing the idea of frequency-sweeping transmission from chirp spread spectrum [S3]. Version D uses a threshold carrier: add a very low, safe-level sine or filtered noise bed that is felt more as pressure/weight than as foreground pitch, while avoiding unsupported claims about actual infrasound effects [S4]. Compare whether the same phrase is heard as more answering, interrupting, suspended, directional, or bodily weighted. Disconfirming evidence: if blind notes show no consistent difference in perceived agency, tension, or direction across carrier variants, then the carrier manipulation did not function as a salient compositional parameter in this setup.

parameters.value: low support bed: 30-45 Hz if playback permits

details.safety: keep below foreground and monitor at safe levels

parameters.value: rising bandpass or pitch-swept carrier layer

details.automation: sweep cutoff or pitch upward during answer

dawChecklist: Write a two-bar MIDI call-and-response phrase at 120 BPM.
Duplicate it into four tracks or scenes with identical notes, velocities, and base harmony.
Carrier A: voice or reharmonize only the answer path using nearest-adjacent harmonic motion.
Carrier B: render response gaps of 0 ms, 300 ms, and 600 ms while keeping notes fixed.
Carrier C: add a rising bandpass/pitch-swept layer under the answer, then print the sweep automation.
Carrier D: add a low, quiet support bed around 30-45 Hz only if the monitoring system can reproduce it safely.
Bounce blind A/B/C/D clips normalized to the same integrated loudness.
Rate each clip for agency, tension, direction, and bodily weight on a 1-5 scale before checking labels.

protocol.listeningContext: nearfield monitors or headphones at safe, matched loudness; avoid excessive low-frequency level
protocol.listeningMethod: blind randomized A/B/C/D comparison with written ratings

notes: Companion essay: docs/essays/the-carrier-under-the-message.md. Keep infrasound claims modest; use the low-frequency bed as a compositional threshold experiment, not a physiological assertion.
